title: Fallback priority transposition causes cross-region/tier misdirect for high-QPS accounts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Several production customers experienced sudden increases in latency and degraded model fidelity when their requests were routed to lower-capacity US-tier variants instead of local EU dedicated pools or compatible hosted variants. This appears correlated with a policy-merge change that altered fallback priority ordering for multi-scope policies (account -> region -> tier).

Impact: Multiple high-QPS accounts (reported by two enterprise customers and internal canary tests) saw up to 40% request routing to suboptimal variants over a 3-hour window, leading to increased latency, token cost, and customer escalations to Support and CSM. Some requests were routed to quantized variants with different model family causing minor hallucination regressions.

Reproduction steps (observed):
1) High-throughput account pinned to model-family X in eu-west with dedicated pool.
2) Simulated brief dedicated saturation (burst > provisioned throughput) + transient region health ping flaps.
3) Smart-routing evaluation returned a fallback list whose priority vector had region and tier entries transposed due to merge order bug.
4) Router selected first compatible entry (US-hosted quantized variant) because transposed ordering placed compatibility above locality.

Root cause (summary): A refactor in policy-merge ordering (PR 7582) introduced a transposition when combining account-level and region-level fallback lists. The merge algorithm stored priority tuples in the wrong index (priority_index vs preference_index) under specific concurrency window where delta policies were applied during reconciliation. This resulted in an effective precedence swap: compatibility>locality for some merged scopes. The bug is deterministic in the presence of non-empty per-region overrides and when policy TTL deltas are applied concurrently.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Immediately rolled back PR 7582 on 2026-03-01 09:12 UTC to stop further divergence.
- Pinned affected customers to their explicit region by setting a soft routing-tie-break to prefer same-region until fix is deployed (admin toggle: routing.enforce_locality=true).
- Enabled an emergency circuit-breaker that prevents fallback to quantized variants for accounts with fidelity SLA flags.

Proposed fix:
1) Correct the merge routine to preserve stable precedence ordering: account-level overrides should append after region-level preferences, not replace index positions. Add unit tests covering concurrent delta application and TTL boundary cases.
2) Add a deterministic comparator used by policy-merge that explicitly encodes (locality_priority, tier_priority, compatibility_score) and write property-based tests.
3) Backfill integration tests that simulate high-concurrency policy reconciliations and assert no precedence inversion.

Deployment plan:
- Code fix + unit tests (ENG) -> gate in staging (canary with 10% of internal traffic including the previously affected accounts) -> monitor for 48 hours.
- After clean canary, roll out to 50% production nodes with rollout monitor (alert if cross-region misroute rate > 0.5%).
- Full rollout if stable.

Telemetry & observability changes:
- Emit metric routing.precedence_inversion.count when merged fallback orders differ from canonical comparator.
- Add per-request debug flag (sampled) that logs merged_fallback_vector to datadog/logstore for postmortem.
- Dashboard updates: routing -> misroute-rate by account/region/tier.

Tests required:
- Unit: merge comparator invariants, index stability.
- Integration: integration test harness that simulates policy deltas and verifies order.
- E2E: synthetic high-QPS replay with injected dedicated saturation to validate fallback selection.

Stakeholders & notifications:
- Eng: Marco Diaz (owner), Priya Nair (code review), Jo Chen (infra validation).
- Product/Support: Lina Morales (PM), Support on-call notified for customer comms.
- Security/Compliance: notified but no PII exposure.

Customer communication:
- Support to send acknowledgement and mitigation summary to impacted accounts; CSM-led follow-up with tech write-up and SLA credit discussion.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests added and green.
- Canary for 48 hours with misroute-rate <= 0.1%.
- Routing.precedence_inversion metric at 0 for 7 days post-rollout.
- Customer escalations closed with resolution note and postmortem.

Notes: The incident highlighted a gap in our policy-merge testing surface for concurrent updates and TTL boundary cases. Follow-up tickets recommended to harden policy reconciliation and add more chaos tests for region reconciliation and capacity flaps.
